observations.statement: Remote LSP transport is stdio tunneled through SSH, follows an explicit establish-spawn-connect-initialize-ready sequence, and operates directly on the remote filesystem without a local mirror.
The connection-loss behavior exposes named GUI choices, marks all affected remote LSP servers degraded, attempts reconnect and reinitialization, and conditionally replays pending requests.

Remote mutations have named effective modes, use FileSafe confirmation and failure reporting, and project server-originated data through a host-aware path mapping before editor or FileSafe consumption.
Normal feature traffic is restricted to Ready sessions, while LspSupervisor and DocumentStore form the authoritative open-buffer and pending-sync boundary.
Document-scoped response applicability is gated by session epoch, URI, current version, and request generation, while one DocumentStore-backed mapper owns UI-to-LSP coordinate conversion.
The core specifies canonical LSP configuration keys and later locks app/project precedence plus scalar, object, array, and inheritance merge behavior.
Virtual Chat documents have a dedicated non-disk URI, attach to the effective host-aware session, and have explicit per-block identity and didOpen/didClose invariants.
ServerSpec is declared the canonical catalog record, and the effective catalog is a deduplicated multi-source union with user settings layered over it.
The core contains both a ten-phase implementation table and a separate appendix acceptance model organized as four phases.

candidate_findings.title: Session-key membership is internally inconsistent
candidate_findings.problem: The prose declares the live attach/session key to be `(host_id, server_id, root_identity)`, but the conceptual `LspSessionKey` adds `project_id`; later spawn flow again uses the three-part key.
candidate_findings.consequence: Implementations can disagree about whether two projects sharing the same host, server, and root reuse one process and state projection or remain isolated by project.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The authoritative equality, persistence, and lookup membership of `LspSessionKey`, including the role of `project_id`, is not fixed.

candidate_findings.title: Lifecycle vocabulary and transition model do not share one state enum
candidate_findings.problem: The canonical user/state names include `RestartBackoff` and `ShuttingDown` but not `crashed`; the separate state chain and transition table use lowercase `stopping` and `crashed` and omit an explicit `RestartBackoff` transition.
candidate_findings.consequence: UI projection, persisted state, capability gating, and supervisor transitions can encode different states or map the same event differently.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: A single normative enum and an exact mapping from process events and backoff activity to every canonical user-visible state is absent.

candidate_findings.title: SSH reconnect and server restart budgets are not related
candidate_findings.problem: Remote reconnect authority permits one bounded automatic retry before explicit Reconnect, while unexpected server-process death permits three restart attempts with 2s/4s/8s backoff; `restart_budget` is modeled without a stated reset or ownership rule.
candidate_findings.consequence: A connection loss that also terminates remote server processes can consume one budget, both budgets, or a fresh budget after reinitialization depending on implementation.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The separation, composition, persistence, and reset conditions for SSH retry and LSP process restart budgets are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Safe replay after SSH reconnect has no exact eligibility contract
candidate_findings.problem: Pending requests are said to be replayed “when safe,” while request validity is session-epoch and generation scoped and request classes have different queue rules; no replay matrix identifies which pending operations survive reinitialization.
candidate_findings.consequence: Soft queries may be lost unnecessarily, while navigation or editing operations may be duplicated or executed against a new session epoch without uniform behavior.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Replay eligibility, epoch reassignment, cancellation, ordering, and treatment of each soft, navigation, and editing request class are not defined.

candidate_findings.title: Stale-response retry policy is contradictory
candidate_findings.problem: The normative stale-response paragraph says not to automatically re-request, but the implementation checklist permits “discard or re-request” on a stale document version.
candidate_findings.consequence: Builders can produce materially different network load and user-visible freshness behavior while each follows one stated instruction.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The authoritative stale-response action, including whether any request class may auto-reissue, is unresolved.

candidate_findings.title: Successful-save notification behavior remains modal
candidate_findings.problem: The buffer-authority contract permits `didSave` only after a successful current-version save, another rule says a successful save “may” emit it, and the implementation phases require didSave implementation without giving the condition that selects emission.
candidate_findings.consequence: Servers may observe different post-save synchronization behavior for the same successful save.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The exact capability or policy predicate that makes `didSave` required, optional, or suppressed is absent.

candidate_findings.title: workspaceFolders selection is not fully deterministic or reconciled with singular root identity
candidate_findings.problem: The session key contains one `root_identity`, while initialization may send up to ten roots; overflow must be excluded deterministically, but no ordering or tie-break rule identifies which ten roots are retained or how they relate to the session root.
candidate_findings.consequence: Equivalent open-document sets can initialize different folders or spawn different session topologies across implementations.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The root ordering, overflow tie-break, and mapping between `root_identity` and the `workspaceFolders` list are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Virtual-document activation and eviction remain discretionary
candidate_findings.problem: Creation is triggered by focus or hover, the lifecycle permits several close triggers or an implementation-selected idle timeout and optional recent-document retention, while the implementer contract names hover/definition as the didOpen trigger.
candidate_findings.consequence: The same Chat interaction can create different attachment lifetimes, request cancellation behavior, and server resource usage.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Whether focus alone opens a document and the exact eviction trigger, idle duration, retention capacity, and precedence among scroll, collapse, close, and retention are not locked.

candidate_findings.title: Multi-source ServerSpec deduplication lacks conflict-resolution rules
candidate_findings.problem: The catalog is a deduplicated union of Microsoft, OpenCode, and Puppet Master data and exposes server IDs, aliases, kinds, and many other fields, but the stated resolution order begins only after a catalog base entry already exists.
candidate_findings.consequence: Conflicting source records can yield different canonical IDs, aliases, field values, or classifications before global and project overrides are applied.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The cross-source match key, alias reconciliation, field-level precedence, conflict reporting, and provenance-preservation rules for constructing the catalog base entry are absent.

candidate_findings.title: Global-disable configuration has two unmapped forms
candidate_findings.problem: The canonical schema defines `lsp.enabled`, while the checklist says to honor `lsp: false`; only the per-server legacy alias receives an explicit read/write mapping.
candidate_findings.consequence: A global disable setting can be accepted, ignored, or serialized differently depending on which form a builder treats as authoritative.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The validity, precedence, and read/write mapping of `lsp: false` relative to `lsp.enabled: false` are not stated.

candidate_findings.title: Arbitrary environment configuration is not reconciled with credential-storage prohibition
candidate_findings.problem: Credentials are required to stay in system keychain or agent flows rather than configuration, but each server accepts an `env` object with no rule distinguishing literal credential values from safe values or references.
candidate_findings.consequence: One implementation may persist secrets in configuration while another cannot represent environment-based authenticated launches.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The allowed `env` value model, secret-reference mechanism, redaction behavior, and validation boundary are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Remote timeout and resource-limit semantics are incomplete
candidate_findings.problem: Remote operations receive a default 3x timeout multiplier, request timeouts are independently user-configurable, memory is described as configurable without a named key, and CPU time has a separate 30s limit without an enforcement outcome.
candidate_findings.consequence: Implementations can multiply different timeout classes, apply different ceilings, and respond differently to memory or CPU overruns.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The multiplier scope and order, resource-limit configuration keys, CPU-versus-wall-clock interpretation, and supervisor transition or error action on limit breach are absent.

candidate_findings.title: Canonical URI and remote path-mapping invariants lack operative normalization rules
candidate_findings.problem: The core forbids duplicate identities caused by case, slash/drive-letter, URI spelling, session pairing, or conversion differences and requires host-aware path mapping, but it does not define normalization inputs, platform rules, canonical output, or mapping failure behavior.
candidate_findings.consequence: Equivalent paths can still produce duplicate document identities or project diagnostics and edits onto the wrong host-scoped document.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The exact URI canonicalization and host-aware path-mapping algorithm, including case sensitivity, drive letters, authority binding, unsupported mappings, and errors, is not specified.

candidate_findings.title: Diagnostics cache identity is expressed in competing forms
candidate_findings.problem: Diagnostics are said to remain per `(server/session, uri)` and per `(session, uri)` in the same rule, while request close handling clears per `(server/session, uri)`; the slash notation is not defined as synonym, choice, or composite.
candidate_findings.consequence: Caches can be keyed, merged, invalidated, and cleared differently across restart or multi-server attachment paths.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: One canonical diagnostics key and exact invalidation behavior for close, crash, reconnect, and session-epoch replacement are absent.

candidate_findings.title: Automatic completion trigger rules conflict
candidate_findings.problem: One section says completion triggers on typing all characters, while the locked behavior says server-advertised trigger characters are used when present and normal typing is the fallback when no trigger characters are advertised.
candidate_findings.consequence: Clients can either send completion requests on every keystroke or only on negotiated triggers for the same server.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The precedence between all-character typing, advertised trigger characters, manual invocation, and the resulting `CompletionContext.triggerKind` is unresolved.

candidate_findings.title: Two incompatible phase taxonomies share the same phase numbers
candidate_findings.problem: The implementation table defines Phases 1 through 10, with Phase 1 as Foundation and Phase 2 as Spawn and lifecycle, while appendix acceptance defines Phases 1 through 4 with Phase 1 covering core interactive LSP and Phase 2 covering navigation and editing.
candidate_findings.consequence: A phase number, completion report, or gate receipt cannot identify a unique deliverable set without additional interpretation.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: An authoritative phase taxonomy or an explicit mapping between the ten-phase table and four-phase appendix is absent.

candidate_findings.title: Acceptance criteria reuse a session key declared stale
candidate_findings.problem: The remote identity rules retain `(server_id, root)` only as migration contrast, yet the Phase 2 deliverable requires spawning per `(id, root)`; the later checklist returns to `(host_id, server_id, root_identity)`.
candidate_findings.consequence: A build can satisfy the phase row with local-only process identity while violating host isolation required by the live session contract.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The Phase 2 deliverable and acceptance criterion are not normatively restated with the live host-aware key.

candidate_findings.title: Mandatory remote MVP behavior lacks corresponding acceptance evidence
candidate_findings.problem: Remote LSP is described as MVP and remote provisioning, placement, scaling, and change annotation are implementation-relevant MVP requirements, but the complete phase table and appendix done criteria contain no remote connection-loss, host-mapping, degraded-mode, provisioning, or remote-scaling acceptance case.
candidate_findings.consequence: The documented acceptance path can mark LSP implementation complete without executable evidence for mandatory remote behavior.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Remote-specific acceptance outcomes and failure evidence for the declared MVP requirements are absent from the shown completion criteria.

candidate_findings.title: Internal section references point to different subjects
candidate_findings.problem: Virtual documents are defined in §14.8 but the later lock points to §14.7, and the config schema is under §14.5 while the prerequisite says to document and consult §14.4.
candidate_findings.consequence: Implementers and generated traceability can resolve a requirement to workspaceFolders or message flow instead of the intended virtual-document or configuration contract.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The normative internal section targets are not consistently identified.

candidate_findings.title: Remote effective modes are not mapped to lifecycle and projection dimensions
candidate_findings.problem: The core names `full_remote_lsp`, `degraded_remote_diagnostics_only`, and `remote_edit_no_lsp`, while the session projection separately carries lifecycle, freshness, health, requested/effective enabled, and capability fields and the lifecycle has a broad `Degraded` state.
candidate_findings.consequence: GUI labels and mutation guards can derive different effective behavior from the same outage or disabled state.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The exact mapping and transition rules between each remote effective mode and every projection/lifecycle field are absent.

candidate_findings.title: Offline cached mode lacks a validation and reconciliation contract
candidate_findings.problem: The GUI may offer cached-file offline work only when a validated cache exists, and open buffers may retain local text and pending-sync state without implying write success, but cache validity, permitted operations, queueing, and reconnect reconciliation are not specified.
candidate_findings.consequence: Offline editing and later reconnect can expose inconsistent mutation affordances or conflicting assumptions about whether local text will synchronize remotely.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The validated-cache predicate, offline capability matrix, pending-sync durability, conflict behavior, and reconnect outcome are absent.

candidate_findings.title: The implementation-closure assertion coexists with unresolved implementation choices
candidate_findings.problem: The core categorically states that no core runtime LSP behavior remains implementation-defined while virtual-document lifetime explicitly allows optional retention and an implementation-selected timeout, and workspace overflow requires deterministic selection without defining the ordering.
candidate_findings.consequence: Builders can treat consequential behavior as discretionary while still claiming compliance with the closure statement.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The closure assertion does not delimit or resolve the remaining optional and unspecified runtime determinants.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Remote LSP explicitly forbids a hidden local sync or mirror and defines parity as explicit capability state rather than hidden local fallback.
Remote preview-worthy and multi-file mutations explicitly use the FileSafe confirmation path, report per-file partial failure, and expose reason copy for unavailable targets.
The authoritative open-buffer source and the condition that must precede any didSave are explicitly assigned to LspSupervisor plus DocumentStore.
LSP I/O is explicitly asynchronous, Slint UI updates are routed through the event loop, and blocking the UI is forbidden.
The response-acceptance contract explicitly requires a live session epoch, matching URI and current document version, and the latest relevant request generation.
Position encoding has an explicit UTF-16 compatibility baseline and one centralized DocumentStore-backed conversion boundary rather than per-feature code-unit math.
App/project configuration precedence and scalar, object, array, and inheritance merge behavior are explicitly locked.
workspace/applyEdit, rename, and code actions explicitly share the FileSafe mutation path and cannot bypass policy or blocked-state reporting.
The virtual-document implementer contract explicitly fixes non-disk URIs, one identity per block instance, host-aware session attachment, and didOpen/didClose boundary events.
After a catalog base entry exists, the effective resolution order through global override, project override, runtime availability, and effective-state evaluation is explicit.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_text: - transport is stdio over SSH; the remote LSP server stdin/stdout are tunneled through the SSH connection rather than exposed by port forwarding
- connection lifecycle is: SSH connection established → remote LSP server spawned → stdio streams connected → initialize handshake → ready
- remote LSP uses the remote filesystem directly; there is no hidden local sync or mirror for LSP operations

On connection-loss, LSP state follows the FileManager/GUI pattern: show `Connection lost`, offer `Reconnect` or `Work offline (cached files only)` when a validated cache exists, keep credentials in system keychain/agent flows rather than config, and expose keep-alive/backoff state through `ssh_connections` compatibility lineage or the current SSH remote profile model.
- if SSH disconnects, all remote LSP servers on that connection are marked `degraded`, reconnect is attempted, servers are re-initialized, and pending requests are replayed when safe
- remote LSP has higher latency by design; PM applies a timeout multiplier for remote operations (default `3x`)

`GitHub_Integration.md §C.3-C.4` / `C.3-C.4` is the operational reconnect authority: keep the 30s keepalive, allow one bounded auto-retry (`one-auto-retry` in older notes), then require explicit `Reconnect`.

- The canonical remote working-folder identity is `user@host:remote/path`; `remote-host`, `working-folder`, and path authority are part of the project/runtime identity. Puppet Master must not create a hidden local `/mirror`, must not silently retarget `/multi-context` work to the local host, and must fail unsupported remote/multi-context launches deterministically with a visible `/risk` reason.

- The stale local-only phrase `(server_id, root)` is retained only as migration contrast. Live LSP attach/session keys are `(host_id, server_id, root_identity)`, and remote documents use host-scoped `/path-mapping` so a file-local URI on host A cannot collide with the same path on host B.

- Diagnostics storage remains per `(server/session, uri)` and per `(session, uri)` and is merged only in presentation. Editor markers and `/gutter` are file-local projections; Problems owns `/merging`; Assistant/Interview and Search consume `/completion/definition/diagnostics`, `/symbols`, and status summaries without becoming the LSP owner.

- Remote install `/provisioning`, `/SSH` placement, large-workspace scaling, and change-annotation behavior are implementation-relevant MVP requirements. Remote LSP stays the same architecture as local LSP, with different host/provisioning/path identity, rather than becoming a second subsystem.

- Remote mutation and availability modes are user-visible. Preview-worthy rename, multi-file code-action, and broad format operations require the same safe preview `/confirmation` path as other FileSafe edits; partial workspace-edit failure reports per-file results, and read-only, locked, unavailable, or `/degraded` targets fail with explicit reason copy. Remote effective modes include `full_remote_lsp`, `degraded_remote_diagnostics_only`, and `remote_edit_no_lsp`; unsupported local-LSP-on-remote-paths behavior must not masquerade as `on-remote-paths` correctness.

- Remote host-placement is explicit: server-originated paths, diagnostics, code actions, and workspace edits are interpreted in the effective remote host context, then passed through host-aware `/path-mapping` before any editor/FileSafe projection. `/degraded/unavailable` remote states keep `/revert/editor`, save, rename, format, and code-action affordances visible only when the same FileSafe and remote write-availability checks would allow the mutation.

- Remote outages affect adjacent consumers without redefining them. Prior Search results may remain as stale snapshots, while new queries that need remote round-trips block or show unavailable; Source Control may expose stale status or `/diff` but must not silently fall back to local Git; Problems and LSP diagnostics may remain visible only when marked stale or unavailable; open remote buffers may retain local text and `/offline/pending-sync` state without implying remote write success. Hunk-level `/diff` interaction, fallback-open actions, read-only reasons, and remote LSP disable/defer decisions use the same capability vocabulary.

- Remote/local parity covers save/dirty state, file watches/reload, diff generation and compare targets, LSP execution/fallback, and rich previews `/renderers`; parity means explicit capability state, not hidden local fallback.

LspSessionProjection {
  key
  lifecycle_state
  freshness
  health
  requested_enabled
  effective_enabled
  capability_summary
  restart_budget
  last_error
}

Canonical user/state names are `Starting`, `Initializing`, `Ready`, `RestartBackoff`, `Degraded`, `ShuttingDown`, and `Stopped`. Only `Ready` emits normal feature traffic; `Starting` and `Initializing` may queue sync work, `RestartBackoff` exposes countdown plus last error, and `Degraded` can mean paused recovery or diagnostics-only / diagnostics-only attachment. Each document is attached once per session, including virtual-doc buffers, and `didClose` is emitted when the final attachment for that `(session, uri)` disappears. The session/model boundary records `/URI` identity so virtual-doc and real-file URI values do not collide.

The `/supervision` boundary is `LspSupervisor` plus `DocumentStore`: `/document-pane` surfaces, editor tabs, chat virtual documents, restore/reload, and `/revert` all consume the same authoritative buffer and pending-sync state. LSP never reads a second document authority for an open file, and `didSave` is emitted only after the shared document store records a successful save for the current version.
States: `stopped → starting → initializing → ready → degraded → stopping → crashed`

| ready | stopping | last file of language closed / user request | send `shutdown` + `exit` |
| stopping | stopped | server process exits | cleanup resources |
| any | crashed | server process dies unexpectedly | log error, attempt restart |
| crashed | starting | auto-restart (max 3 attempts, backoff 2s/4s/8s) | respawn |
| crashed | stopped | restart limit exceeded | show error, require manual restart |

- max memory per server is configurable, default `512MB`
- max CPU time for a single request is `30s`

1. **User opens file** → Editor loads buffer → Resolve (path → extension → server id → effective host/root identity) → If server not running for `(host_id, server_id, root_identity)`, spawn process → Initialize handshake → Send `didOpen` with content + version.
All LSP I/O on **async task** (tokio); route UI updates to the Slint event loop (e.g. via `slint::invoke_from_event_loop` or `Weak::upgrade_in_event_loop`). Never block UI on LSP.
**Do not** automatically re-request; the user can repeat the action (e.g. hover again, trigger completion again) to get a fresh result.

Document identity, freshness, and `/position` conversion are one contract. Before `didClose`, PM cancels in-flight document-scoped requests for `(session, uri)` and clears diagnostics per `(server/session, uri)`. Each document-scoped request carries `session_epoch`, `uri`, `document_version`, and `request_generation` or an equivalent latest-of-class marker; responses apply only for the same live session epoch, same URI, matching current document version, and latest relevant request class. Late replies are discarded in UX but remain visible in trace `/logs`.

At open time, PM creates one canonical `DocumentUri` per document/host and reuses it consistently. The same physical file must not gain duplicate identities through case, `/slash/drive-letter`, URI spelling, `(session, uri)` pairing, or `/path/position` conversion differences. UI/editor surfaces stay 1-based where already planned; the LSP boundary remains 0-based and uses one position-mapper / position-mapping service backed by `DocumentStore`. `capabilities.positionEncoding` and `position_encoding` are negotiated per session; PM uses compatibility-first position-encoding, keeps UTF-16 as the guaranteed baseline, may prefer `utf-8` only after compatibility proof, and must not hard-code UTF assumptions into hover, `/completion/diagnostics/rename`, diagnostics, rename, or formatting handlers. Conversion uses fast per-line helpers/cache so multi-server correctness, remote `/SSH`, and performance tuning stay protocol-safe.

LSP coordinates use the protocol's code-unit conventions at the boundary; the centralized conversion layer records whether a server uses UTF-16 code-unit offsets, another negotiated encoding, or compatibility fallback, so individual feature handlers never hand-roll code-unit math.

- Sync events are FIFO per session. A document-scoped request must not leave the queue until the target session is `Ready`, the prior `didOpen`/`didChange` work for that document in that session has flushed, and the document is no longer in pending-sync state.

- Hover, `/completion/signatureHelp`, and similar soft requests keep only the newest pending request per document `/request-class`; older in-flight or not-yet-ready requests are canceled or dropped on `/close`, cursor movement, or newer input.
- Explicit navigation and editing requests such as definition, references, rename, format, and `codeAction` wait behind the sync barrier once and then execute only if still relevant.

- `didChange` debounce is resetting `/coalescing`, not fixed-window batching. All mutations since the last sent sync for that session/doc become one batch; if incremental confidence is lost, send a whole-document replacement to re-baseline; if confidence is still not trustworthy, restart the session and replay currently attached docs.
- A successful save may emit `didSave` for the current document version/content state. Failed save does not emit `didSave`, and stale-result handling must not make the UI look saved or synchronized.

- **Keys:** `lsp.enabled` (bool, default true), `lsp.servers.<id>.disabled` (bool), `lsp.servers.<id>.command` (string array), `lsp.servers.<id>.extensions` (string array), `lsp.servers.<id>.env` (object), `lsp.servers.<id>.initialization` (object). **Decision:** Config namespace is `lsp.servers.<id>.*`; support legacy alias `lsp.<id>.disabled` (read/write maps to `lsp.servers.<id>.disabled`). Align with OpenCode schema for compatibility.

- **Debounce / timeouts:** Store in Settings → Editor or Developer: `lsp.didChangeDebounceMs` (default **100**, range 50-500), `lsp.hoverTimeoutMs` (default **5000**), `lsp.completionTimeoutMs` (default **5000**), `lsp.workspaceSymbolTimeoutMs` (default **10000**), `lsp.hoverDelayMs` (default **300**, range 100-1000, delay before sending hover request). All timeouts user-configurable. Document in implementation guide.
- **Completion:** Trigger on typing (all characters) or on explicit shortcut (e.g. Ctrl+Space). Send `CompletionContext` with `triggerKind`: Invoked or TriggerCharacter.

- **Recommendation:** At initialize, send **only roots that have at least one open document**, capped at **10** roots. If user has no open files, send project root if single-root, else empty list. Reduces startup cost and memory; document in implementation guide. Re-initialize not required when opening a file in a new root; the matching host-aware server session handles that.
### 14.8 Virtual documents (Chat code blocks)

- **Creation:** When the user focuses or hovers over a code block in a Chat message that has a known language id and the project has an LSP server for that language, create a virtual document: assign a URI, set content to the block text, and attach it to the **server for that language and the effective host/root identity for the current project context** (same session that would handle a real file with that extension). If the block maps to a real project file (e.g. "snippet from src/main.rs"), use the real file URI instead and do not create a virtual doc.

- **Lifecycle:** Send `textDocument/didOpen` when the virtual document is "opened" (e.g. when the user first hovers or requests definition in that block). Send `textDocument/didClose` when the block is no longer needed: when the user scrolls away from that message, when the message is collapsed, or when the Chat view is closed; or after T seconds idle (e.g. 300 s) if implementing eviction by timeout. Optionally retain a bounded set of recently used virtual docs (e.g. last 5) to avoid repeated didOpen/didClose on quick hover. Do not send `didChange` for virtual docs (blocks are immutable); if the user edits the message and the block content changes, treat as a new block (new opaque_id) and close the old virtual doc.

- **Contract for implementer:** (1) Virtual URI never points to disk; (2) one virtual doc per code block instance (same block in UI = same opaque_id); (3) didOpen is sent when the block needs LSP (hover/definition); (4) didClose is sent when the block is evicted or the view is closed; (5) hover/definition requests for that block use the virtual URI and the same `(host_id, server_id, root_identity)` as for that language in the current project context.
`ServerSpec` is the canonical machine-friendly catalog record for both built-in and custom servers.

- `server_id`
- `display_name`
- `sources[]` (`microsoft`, `opencode`, `pm` for catalog provenance; custom rows use `kind = custom`)
- `source_names[]` / `aliases[]`
- `kind` (`managed_builtin`, `managed_catalog`, `custom`)

- the effective support catalog is the deduped union of Microsoft implementor data, OpenCode catalog data, and Puppet Master overlay metadata
- user enable/disable and custom-server settings layer on top of the catalog instead of replacing it
- derived prose tables and `/readable` `/settings/docs` views may be generated from this support-catalog registry, but this structure remains the SSOT and prevents the large union catalog from becoming duplicate-prone prose
- Support scope and support classification stay separate in the `/catalog`: supported-by-registry, default-managed, toolchain-bound `/manual`, experimental `/degraded`, and deprecated or `/replaced` are classification outcomes layered over stable `server_id` identity, not reasons to fork the catalog SSOT. Effective resolution order is catalog base entry, global override, project override, then runtime availability and `/effective-state` evaluation.

| Phase | Deliverables | Acceptance criteria |
|-------|--------------|---------------------|
| **1. Foundation** | LSP client crate integrated; server registry (in-memory); config loading (lsp.* from redb/config). | App starts; config can disable LSP globally; registry returns server id by extension. |
| **2. Spawn and lifecycle** | Spawn server process per (id, root); stdio transport; initialize handshake; shutdown/exit on close. | Opening a `.rs` file (with rust-analyzer in PATH) spawns one process; closing all files in that root shuts down server. |
| **3. Document sync** | didOpen, didChange (debounced), didClose, didSave; version tracking; incremental sync when server supports. | Editing file sends didChange after debounce; version increments; no flood of messages. |

### Canonical config location and precedence
App-level configuration lives under `config.lsp`.

Project overrides live at `.puppet-master/lsp.json`.

Merge order:
1. app-level `config.lsp`
2. project override `.puppet-master/lsp.json`

Merge rules:
- scalar keys override
- object keys override by nested key
- arrays replace rather than merge
- absent keys inherit
- server-specific settings resolve by server id first, then by language/filetype mapping only when no explicit server-id override exists

| `didChangeDebounceMs` | `100` |
| `hoverTimeoutMs` | `5000` |
| `completionTimeoutMs` | `5000` |
| `workspaceSymbolTimeoutMs` | `10000` |
| `hoverDelayMs` | `300` |
| `workspaceFolders` cap | `10` roots with at least one open document |

- completion uses server-advertised trigger characters when provided
- when a server does not advertise trigger characters, completion still supports normal typing plus explicit manual invocation
- inlay hints refresh on document open and after debounced `didChange`
- scroll-only refresh is not required for MVP
- hover uses the canonical `hoverDelayMs` and `hoverTimeoutMs` values above
Only roots containing at least one open document are included, up to the cap above. Overflow roots are excluded deterministically and MUST be visible in logs/evidence when exclusion affects behavior.

`workspace/applyEdit`, rename, and code-action application use the same FileSafe-backed apply-edit path as other agent mutations.
- multi-file edits are treated as multi-file mutations
- destructive edits use the same safety and approval rules as any other file mutation path
- LSP does not bypass FileSafe, tool policy, or blocked-state reporting
Chat/code-block virtual documents keep the existing virtual-document stance already defined in §14.7. This section does not reopen that decision.
No core runtime LSP behavior remains implementation-defined after this section.
